# XslTransformationFailureConsumed

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Identify transformToXML result on a resolved XSLTProcessor passed directly or unchanged to file_put_contents or echo without rejecting false.

## Detection

- D1. Report transformToXML result on a resolved XSLTProcessor passed directly or unchanged to file_put_contents or echo without rejecting false.
- D2. Resolve builtin functions, classes, constants and methods, including imports and supported named arguments. Follow only bounded local facts within one lexical scope. Receiver and argument provenance must establish the specific API contract; variable names and comments never prove intent.
- D4. A value counts as having rejected false when the use is dominated by a test of the same unchanged value that cannot pass for false:
  - a strict comparison with `false` (`!== false` branch, or a terminating `=== false` guard);
  - a truthiness test (`if ($out)`, `if (!$out) { return; }`, `empty($out)`), since false and null are both falsy;
  - a loose comparison with `false` (`!= false` branch, terminating `== false` guard);
  - a resolved builtin `is_string()` test.
  The test may be the condition of an enclosing `if`/`elseif`/`else` branch or ternary arm, the left operand of a short-circuit `&&`/`||`/`and`/`or` whose right operand holds the use, or an earlier sibling `if` without `else`/`elseif` whose body always terminates. Negation, parentheses, conjunctions (for the passing side) and disjunctions (for the failing side) are followed. An assignment of the call inside the condition is the tested value.
- D3. Report one finding per violating operation. A reachable path, unchanged value identity and applicable API behavior are required. Intervening mutation, unknown calls involving tracked values, escaped aliases or exhausted analysis budgets invalidate proof.

## Exceptions (no report)

- E1. Exclude unresolved required symbols, user-defined lookalikes, incomplete syntax, unknown required values and unsupported versions. Cases outside D1 receive no finding.
- E3. A guard on a different value, on an earlier transformation result that was since reassigned, or on a test that false can pass (`isset`, `!== null`, `is_string(...) || ...`) does not suppress the finding.
- E4. A value the shared flow analysis proves is not false at the use is never reported, whatever form the proof takes: a truthiness or `empty()` test, a loose comparison with `false` or `null`, a type predicate, or an early exit whose `if` also has an `else` branch that continues. In particular `if (!$out) { return; } else { ... }` guards the statements after it. The same holds for a statement that leaves on the failing outcome (`$v !== false or exit;`, `$v or throw …;`, `$v ?: throw …;`), for a failing branch that ends in a call that never returns (a callee declared `never`, or a function or a final or private method every path of which throws or exits), for a test stored in a boolean and tested later while neither the boolean nor the tested variable has been written, and, on PHP 8.0 and later outside any `try` with a `catch`, for a builtin call that returned after receiving the value for a parameter that only accepts arrays, objects or callables: such a call throws a `TypeError` for `false`. A `switch (true)` case is read like the condition of an `if`/`elseif` chain. Positions PHP may skip prove nothing: the right side of `??=`, the arguments of a null-safe call and anything chained after `?->`. A null-safe call to a never-returning method does not end the path, and `f(...)` creates a closure without calling `f`.
- E2. Both `@custos-ignore XslTransformationFailureConsumed` and `@noinspection XslTransformationFailureConsumed` suppress this native rule.

## Fix

None. A repair requires a semantic decision or application error-handling policy.

## PHP versions

Available in PHP 5.3–8.5 where the referenced API exists. Do not apply extension contracts when the resolved API is unavailable. Gate syntax and version-specific behavior to the configured target.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "XslTransformationFailureConsumed": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore XslTransformationFailureConsumed
```
